specification.problem: Construct f-controlled phase gates for a three-qubit refined Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm from sigma_z, two-qubit controlled-phase and two-target controlled-phase gates. The abstract does not give the explicit decomposition or the circuit QED implementation details.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful construction: the generic phase-oracle form of the refined DJ algorithm on 3 qubits, and the diagonal phase gate for one example function f, decomposed into Z, CZ and CCZ-type gates. Outside scope: the paper's specific decomposition of all 35 gates, the transmon-qutrit/cavity Hamiltonian, pulse sequences, and numerical feasibility simulations.

symbols.meaning: controlled-controlled phase gate, here taken as an example of a multi-qubit phase gate

equations.label: f-controlled phase gate
equations.description: Diagonal phase oracle for a Boolean function f.
equations.abstract_quote: f$-controlled phase gates of a three-qubit refined Deutsch-Jozsa (DJ) algorithm
equations.justification: The name f-controlled phase gate suggests a phase determined by f(x); the sign convention is assumed.
assumptions: Phase is (-1)^{f(x)}, the standard DJ phase-oracle convention

equations.label: DJ circuit amplitude
equations.description: Standard DJ output amplitude on the all-zero state: magnitude 1 for constant f and 0 for balanced f.
equations.justification: Textbook DJ algorithm. The paper's refined variant may differ in details not given in the abstract.
assumptions: Standard single-query phase-oracle DJ circuit used as a proxy for the refined version

equations.label: Phase gate as polynomial in x
equations.description: The algebraic normal form of f makes U_f a product of Z (|S|=1), CZ (|S|=2) and CCZ (|S|=3) gates, with a global sign for S empty.
equations.justification: Every Boolean function has a unique ANF. This is a generic decomposition, not necessarily the paper's protocol, which uses two-target controlled phase gates.
assumptions: Generic decomposition; the paper's two-target gates are not reproduced

equations.label: Example instance
equations.description: A tiny balanced example function with its decomposition into one single-qubit Z and one two-qubit CZ.
equations.justification: Chosen as an illustrative instance; it is not claimed to be from the paper.
assumptions: Example f chosen by the reconstruction
f is balanced, so the all-zero amplitude is 0

registers.name: q
registers.role: Three computational qubits, ordered q1q2q3, with x=4x_1+2x_2+x_3

steps.description: Apply Hadamard to each qubit to prepare the uniform superposition.
Apply the f-controlled phase gate U_f, decomposed into Z, CZ and CCZ gates according to the ANF of f (example: Z_1 CZ_23).
Apply Hadamard to each qubit again.

specification.measurement: Measure all three qubits in the computational basis. Under the standard DJ assumption, outcome 000 indicates constant f and any other outcome indicates balanced f.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Declare f constant if the result is 000, otherwise balanced.
assumptions: No scope was supplied, so a single oracle instance was chosen
Standard DJ phase-oracle convention used in place of the paper's refined algorithm
The paper's decomposition into 35 gates is not reconstructed
missing_information: Definition of the refined DJ algorithm and the set of 35 functions
The explicit gate decomposition and the two-target controlled-phase construction
Transmon qutrit/cavity Hamiltonian, pulse timings, and decoherence parameters
